definitions.explanation: One of the small leaf-like segments that together form the calyx of a flower. Sepals wrap the bud before it opens and usually stay attached, green and inconspicuous, behind the petals.

examples.japanese: {萼片|がくへん}が{五|ご}{枚|まい}ある。
この{花|はな}の{萼片|がくへん}は{緑色|みどりいろ}で{目立|めだ}たない。
examples.english: The sepals of this flower are green and inconspicuous.

examples.japanese: {萼片|がくへん}が{開|ひら}くと、{中|なか}から{白|しろ}い{花|はな}びらが{見|み}えてきた。
examples.english: When the sepals opened, white petals came into view inside.

notes:
A botanical term, used in textbooks and plant descriptions rather than everyday conversation. The individual segment is the {萼片|がくへん}; the whole ring of them is the {萼|がく}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {萼片|がくへん}が{開|ひら}く: the sepals open
- {萼片|がくへん}が{落|お}ちる: the sepals drop off
- {緑色|みどりいろ}の{萼片|がくへん}: green sepals

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {萼|がく}: calyx — the sepals taken together as one structure
- {花|はな}びら: petal — the colorful segment inside the sepals

cross_references.label: calyx; the sepals as a whole
